n: Hasegawa Store Bay Area (ハセガワストア ベイエリア店)
w: Hakodate's convenience-store institution: the yakitori bentō grilled to order — in southern Hokkaido 'yakitori' means pork.

n: Uni Murakami Hakodate Honten (うに むらかみ 函館本店)
address: Morning-market streets, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan (5 min walk from Hakodate Station)
w: Restaurant of a sea-urchin wholesaler that long supplied Tsukiji and top sushi counters — sweet, additive-free raw uni in bowls and set meals.

dish: Asahikawa shio ramen (gentle paitan, tokusei toroniku)
n: Ramen Santouka Honten, Asahikawa (らーめん山頭火 本店)
w: Hitoshi Hatanaka's nine-seat 1988 shop that took Hokkaido ramen worldwide — a mild, low-salt white broth; the tokusei toroniku (pork-cheek) bowl.

dish: Asahikawa shōyu ramen with burnt lard (kogashi lard)
n: Ramen no Hachiya Gojō Sōgyōten (ラーメンの蜂屋 五条創業店)
w: Since 1947: a pork-bone and dried-horse-mackerel double broth under burnt lard, with house noodles — the shop credited with Asahikawa's low-hydration noodle.

n: Baikōken Honten, Asahikawa (梅光軒 本店)
w: Founded 1969 — pork, chicken and seafood double broth, rich yet clean; first winner of the citizens' Asahikawa Ramen Grand Prize.
